correctness.rationale: Convexity of ||P-J||_op for symmetric stochastic matrices and the H-automorphism and fiber-permutation action proves a global optimizer exists in the two-edge-orbit class. In that class P=I-x L_H tensor I-y I tensor L_{K_s}, with x,y>=0 and d x+(s-1)y<=1. Every nonconstant spectral mode lies between 1-alpha*x, 1-s*y and 1-beta*x-s*y, so the exact objective is max{1-alpha*x,1-s*y,beta*x+s*y-1}. The first two constraints force x>=(1-u)/alpha and y>=(1-u)/s; substituting into the third endpoint and row budget gives M=max{beta+2alpha,2d+2alpha(s-1)/s}; x=2/M,y=2alpha/(sM) attains the bound. Active endpoint or budget yields uniqueness within the invariant class, not among all matrices. Johnson spectrum 0,n,2n-2 gives threshold s(n-3)<n including equality. The proof treats all connected vertex-and-edge-transitive H; finite spectral/LP tests are support only.

value.rationale: A sharp design and holding-phase classification over arbitrary connected edge-and-vertex-transitive base graphs with clique-layer augmentation, including a concrete Johnson-graph integer frontier. The exact weight allocation and universally active spectral/budget constraints resolve an optimization problem, rather than merely displaying a generic SDP formulation.

limitations: Only symmetric nonnegative stochastic supported chains with allowable holding are optimized, not nonreversible mixing or mixing time.
Uniqueness is proved among two-orbit invariant solutions only; other optimal non-orbit-constant matrices may exist.
